title: Choose HAL Notes' visual world
question: The roll assigned the Observatory Atlas. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Observatory Atlas
options.lineage: celestial atlases, observatory consoles, ephemeris tables
options.thesis: The vault as a night sky: notes are catalogued stars, wiki-links are constellation lines, HAL is the observer at the eyepiece. Dense data rendered calmly on a deep sky ground — the tradition of the star atlas, not the dashboard.
options.viewport: The editor as a catalog desk: a deep-blue-black field, the note's title as a catalog entry in a refined grotesk, prose column on a faint hairline grid, the sidebar a star index with magnitude-ordered type; the graph view is the sky chart itself.
options.risk: Astronomical imagery can drift into sci-fi cosplay if the atlas discipline (tables, grids, restraint) is not held.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by luminosity and depth instead of boxes: the front plane is brightest, rear planes recede — panels separate by light, not borders.
Constellation lines carry tension: link weight and staleness render as cord tension in the graph, structure made visible as opposing forces.
States stamp themselves: completed cards and reviewed items get catalog-stamp states (stamped, cancelled) instead of color flips.
One living focus point: the caret and active panel get a faint instrument-lamp bloom; everything else holds still.

options.label: Apollo Avionics
options.lineage: Apollo DSKY, cockpit night lighting, mission-control consoles
options.thesis: The vault as mission instrumentation: state lamps, elastomer-key tactility, single-accent night lighting (amber or green) on near-black, every control labeled like a panel. HAL's native home — the film's own consoles.
options.viewport: The app as a night-lit instrument panel: mode switching as panel select lamps, sync status as an annunciator, the editor a lit work surface with panel-divider rules.
options.risk: Avionics-dark is a familiar tech aesthetic; without the lamp discipline it reads as generic dark dashboard.

options.label: Graphite Developer Console
options.thesis: Graphite ground, panels separated by one-pixel seams and one elevation step, syntax-derived accents for state only, destructive actions isolated in deliberate space.
options.viewport: The safest excellent choice: what the app already is, rebuilt with perfect discipline.
options.case: Wins pure task-clarity; identifies with your tools more than with this product's soul.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.lineage: green-phosphor CRTs in midnight machine rooms
options.thesis: One monospaced face on curved glass, cursor bloom, afterimage trails; system states print themselves.
options.viewport: The vault as a living transcript on a green tube.
options.case: Deep audience identification (terminal culture); prose notes and the learning-warmth surfaces suffer under one-face grammar.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: 1960s airline ticket wallets, coupons, route maps
options.thesis: Journeys as coupon books: each learning path tears off leg by leg, states stamp themselves (VALIDATED / VOID), route arcs map the vault.
options.viewport: The research mode as a folded journey wallet; light-first.
options.case: Holds clarity for the learning-path surface narrowly; weaker for daily editor density.

options.label: Baseline Dust Field
options.thesis: Ivory bitmap baselines on an emissive void; state is depth and drift; nothing is ever boxed.
options.kept: Depth-by-luminosity hierarchy — adopted into the Observatory Atlas as a named raise.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: Structure as opposing forces; annotations pinned to nodes on leader lines.
options.kept: Tension-as-structure for the graph's constellation lines — adopted as a named raise.

options.label: The Category Standard
options.thesis: The familiar polished dark markdown app, played straight and executed at full fidelity.
options.viewport: What every note app ships; your door if the dealt worlds are not this product.

options.label: Re-roll the hand
options.line: A fresh hand from the catalog (plain), safer (conventional + canon), or bolder (foreign forms only) — say which register with your choice.
